bullets.text: Board chair closed the public hearing for DP16-23 Lakeview Farm Inc. at 7:15, after Ken (staff) recommended approval with conditions including 75% open space set-aside and the 50-foot building envelope shift already implemented by the applicant's engineer, Sheila McIntyre.
Board chair closed the public hearing for DP17-30 William and Annie Spencer at 7:58, on the recommendation of board member S4 that this be done prior to deliberation.

No final vote was taken on the Spencer allocation reinstatement; the chair proposed the board would either get a legal opinion or continue the item a month so the applicant, Lot C owner, and staff could resolve the conservation commission's open-space concern before a decision is made.

The board moved into deliberation on Mapletree Place (DP10-35) final plans review after Ken (staff) reported that outstanding items (pedestrian connection, crosswalks, bike rack details, street trees) had been addressed by the applicant.
Ken (staff) acknowledged he may have missed drafting a condition documenting the 50-foot building envelope shift on Lot 2 for the Lakeview Farm application.
Ken flagged that Lisa Shelter (a reviewing department) tends to withhold sign-off unless the applicant provides written responses to all her comments, including a required erosion control plan.

The chair raised concern that the conservation commission's recommendation to protect the southern half of Lot C as open space affects a lot that is not owned by the Spencer applicants and not part of this application, and that the unnotified owner (Scott Gardner) could object.
Ken noted this situation—reallocating growth management units while a conservation commission condition affects a separately owned lot—is unprecedented for the board.

Board member S4 expressed concern that if the Spencer allocation is pushed back into the competitive growth management process, meeting the open-space scoring criteria would be difficult without also securing protection on the abutting Lot C.

The board must decide whether the Spencer/Pumpkin Hill Road subdivision is in "substantial compliance with the intent and purpose of the current development regulations," per Melinda's (staff) special findings criteria.
Whether a legal opinion is needed on the board's ability to impose or enforce an open-space condition on Lot C, which is owned separately from the Spencer's Lot B.
Whether pursuing the conservation commission's recommendation would effectively require the board to treat the Spencer's allocation as leverage over a lot they don't own.
How continuing/tabling the Spencer item would affect the calendar-year deadline for reestablishing the expired growth management allocation.
For Mapletree Place, whether certain landscaping (trees/shrubs) shown within the Velco easement area comply with the height restriction (max ~7 feet).

The conservation commission's 2008 recommendation that the entire southern half of Lot C be protected open space was never implemented in the approved final plans, and Ken (staff) and the chair discussed uncertainty over why, with Ken suggesting it stemmed from early/looser 75% open space rules and the original applicant's resistance to restrictive conditions.

Applicant Annie Spencer questioned whether the board was effectively "holding hostage" her allocation to force compliance on Lot C's owner; the chair pushed back on the characterization, saying they were trying to find a path forward, not hold anything hostage.

Board member S4 argued that pursuing growth management competition would be a near-futile "exercise" for the applicant, while Ken (staff) disagreed, noting the applicant could still score sufficient points on other criteria or receive one of the board's annual exemptions.
Done: Presented staff report on DP16-23 Lakeview Farm Inc., a two-lot split in the ARR district, noting only ~10.6 acres of the 13-acre parcel is in Williston jurisdiction.
Done: Confirmed the 75% open space set-aside requirement applies and that the conservation commission recommended 7.95 acres of open space and no watershed buffers for the class 3 ponds.
Blocker: Acknowledged staff may have missed drafting a condition on shifting the Lot 2 building envelope boundary 50 feet, though the applicant's plan already reflects the change.

Next: Advised applicant to submit a written response to Lisa Shelter (town engineer) addressing underground utilities, right-of-way permit, and the new erosion control plan requirement before final plans can be signed off.
Done: Presented staff analysis on DP17-30 Spencer reallocation request, explaining growth management allocation rules, substantial compliance criteria, and history of the Gardner/Spencer subdivision.

Blocker: Raised the unresolved question of whether the board can/should impose the conservation commission's recommended open space change on Lot C, which is owned by a different party not part of this application.

Done: Clarified for the board that growth management scoring includes exemptions and other criteria beyond open space, so failure to designate open space wouldn't necessarily prevent Lot C from obtaining allocation later.
Done: Reviewed final plans for Mapletree Place amendment #2, confirming pedestrian connections, crosswalks, bike rack details, and street tree locations have been addressed per prior conditions.
Next: Board to review whether landscaping under the Velco easement (e.g., red maple trees) meets height restrictions before finalizing plans.
Done: Confirmed the building envelope on Lot 2 was moved 50 feet from the southern property boundary per the board's prior recommendation.
Done: Reported additional plantings (evergreens and deciduous trees) were added along the northern boundary on Lot 1 as recommended.
Done: Obtained state wastewater and potable water supply permits for both septic systems since the last meeting.
Next: Will provide a written response and erosion control plan to Lisa Shelter to satisfy her outstanding pre-application comments.

Done: Presented pre-application review for DP17-30 (Spencer), explaining the bylaw criteria for reestablishing expired growth management allocation (timing, substantial progress, five-year extension limit).
Done: Reported the conservation commission's recommendation that the entire southern half of Lot C be designated protected open space, which was not implemented in the original 2008 approval.
Blocker: Noted the conservation commission believes the subdivision is not in substantial compliance with current regulations due to the open space configuration, leaving it to the board to decide.
Done: Confirmed the applicants met the time-limitation and substantial-progress criteria (house built, private road constructed) for reinstating allocation.
Done: Noted the fire department's outstanding concerns about driveway grade, curve radius, and a recommended fire pond.
Done: Clarified the application seeks growth management allocation specifically for Lot B (the L-shaped, 16-acre lot with a 2-acre envelope), not Lot C.
Blocker: Raised concern that the board's proposed condition affecting Lot C (owned by another party) could effectively hold the Spencers' allocation hostage since they don't own that lot.
Done: Explained that Lot B was purchased from Scott Gardner three months ago after he decided not to build there, and that they only learned this year the allocation had expired.
Next: Plans to build on Lot B as soon as possible next year, pending resolution of the allocation issue.
Done: Closed DP16-23 Lakeview Farm Inc. at 07:15 after confirming all staff and conservation commission conditions were addressed.
Blocker: Recessed the DP17-30 Spencer hearing because the board had not received Melinda's growth management report in advance and needed copies printed.
Next: Proposed that the board either seek a legal opinion or continue the Spencer application a month to resolve the conflict over the conservation commission's recommendation affecting Lot C.
Done: Closed the DP17-30 Spencer public hearing at 07:58 to allow the board to deliberate.
Next: Board to review Mapletree Place landscaping (tree height under Velco easement) before finalizing conditions of approval.

Agreed to provide a written response to town engineer Lisa Shelter addressing all her pre-application comments, including the newly required erosion control plan, so she will sign off on the final plans checklist for Lakeview Farm Inc.

Acknowledged he had not drafted a condition memorializing the board's prior recommendation to shift the Lot 2 building envelope boundary 50 feet, and needs to correct the findings/conditions accordingly.

Will explore whether the DRB can/should seek a legal opinion on enforcing the conservation commission's open space recommendation on Lot C, which is owned by a party not included in the Spencer (Lot B) allocation application.
Intends to build on Lot B "as soon as possible next year," contingent on the DRB reinstating the expired growth management allocation.

Proposed that, given the conflict between reinstating the Lot B allocation and the conservation commission's recommendation affecting Lot C (owned by someone else), the board should either obtain a legal opinion or continue the application about a month so all parties can meet at the planning office to resolve it before a decision is made.

The DRB still needs to decide whether the Spencer/Gardner 3-lot subdivision is in "substantial compliance with the intent and purpose" of current development regulations in order to reinstate the expired allocation for Lot B.

For Mapletree Place (DP10-35 amendment #2), the board needs to finish reviewing final plan details—paint colors and whether new street trees/landscaping within the Velco easement exceed the height limit—before completing deliberation.

Unresolved question of whether the owner of Lot C (not a party to the Spencer application) will accept or contest the conservation commission's recommendation to convert the southern half of his building envelope to protected open space.
Unclear how reinstating/denying the Lot B allocation would affect the calendar-year deadline for reapplying, since the board took no action and simply continued discussion at the hearing.

Whether trees/shrubs planned in the Mapletree Place parking area landscaping, located inside the Velco easement, comply with the apparent 7-foot height restriction was flagged by the chair but not resolved.

DRB reviewed DP16-23 Lakeview Farm Inc (2-lot split on Oak Hill Rd); building envelope shift and added plantings were confirmed as completed, and the application moved toward approval with conditions.

DRB heard pre-application DP17-30 (William and Annie Spencer, Lot B) seeking to reinstate expired growth management allocation, but got stuck on a Conservation Commission recommendation affecting a neighboring, unowned Lot C, and closed the hearing without a decision.

Board also reviewed final plans/conditions for DP10-35 Amendment 2 (Mapletree Place), confirming applicant addressed pedestrian connections, crosswalks, bike racks, and street trees, then moved into deliberation.

Lakeview Farm Inc: Applicant confirmed the Lot 2 building envelope was moved 50 feet from the southern boundary per prior board recommendation, and additional evergreen/deciduous plantings were added along the northern boundary of Lot 1.

Lakeview Farm Inc: State wastewater/water supply permits have been obtained for both septic systems; applicant still needs to submit erosion control plan and written responses to Lisa Shelter's comments to get her sign-off.
Lakeview Farm Inc public hearing closed at 07:15 with staff recommending approval (findings, conclusions, conditions already drafted).

Mapletree Place: Staff confirmed applicant fixed prior plan deficiencies — pedestrian connection through new parking area, crosswalks at all four intersections, bike rack details/locations, and street trees along new parking areas are now shown on plans.
Spencer/Lot B pre-application hearing was closed at 07:58 per staff advice, with the board deferring its decision on whether the subdivision meets 'substantial compliance' criteria.

Board must decide whether the Spencer/Lot B subdivision (DP17-30) is in 'substantial compliance' with current development regulations to reinstate expired allocation; Conservation Commission wants Lot C's southern half protected as open space, but Lot C is owned by a different party (not part of this application).
Board discussed getting a legal opinion or continuing the Spencer application a month to let applicants, Lot C's owner, and staff resolve the open space/boundary issue together.

Uncertainty remains on whether pursuing the Conservation Commission's recommendation on Lot C could be seen as holding the Spencers' allocation 'hostage'; Ken noted commission is only advisory to the board.
Timing risk: allocation clock resumes and Spencers may need to reapply/compete for growth management points if the board does not act before year-end 2017.
Fire department flagged driveway grade and curve radius concerns and recommended a fire pond for the Spencer subdivision — not yet resolved.
Staff noted Lakeview Farm Inc.'s engineer must still confirm erosion control plan is submitted to Lisa Shelter to finalize her checklist sign-off before final plan approval.
Landscaping height question raised for Mapletree Place: some proposed maple trees within the Velco easement may need to stay under 7 feet — needs verification before final approval.
